## Abstract

‘Global crises and the future of globalization’ assesses how globalization may continue in the twenty-first century. Many problems, ranging from international terrorism to the fallout from the Global Financial Crisis, stalk our world. Will these issues help or hinder international cooperation. On the surface these social processes look hard to stop, but hard times can lead to extremism. Previous attempts to create a global market led to the erosion of social security and the outbreak of World War I. Subsequent protectionism led to fascism and Nazism, resulting in World War II. Inequalities and instability need to be countered to prevent a repeat of history — a Global New Deal is needed.
